ownerStatement: Owner decision (2026-11-08): every analyzer we ship must be onboarded to the LSP/IDE lane, measured, tested, validated and verified — not just the 14 wave-1/wave-2 languages. Wave 3 authorises the remaining 38 languages to be executed through the same protocol; it does NOT pre-claim any of them. Each language's claim is whatever the wave execution measures: PASS when its S5/S6 evidence is verified, otherwise an honest BLOCKED (with the failing check and the analyzer gap) or NOT-LSP-APPROPRIATE (a data/query format where references or call hierarchy are semantically wrong).
authority: The wave protocol (docs/m29/WAVE-PROTOCOL.md) governs: a language joins src/lsp/launch_languages.ts only through a wave approval record, and the wave execution gate judges it on real machinery.
evidenceRule: Approval is authorisation, never evidence. Evidence is the per-language record produced by script/m29/wave-execute.ts (S5) and the in-editor driver (S6); the verifier recomputes the claim from those records.
notes: Ambiguous-extension languages (objc/matlab share .m) are expected to report BLOCKED on path resolution until content sniffing lands; guessing an identity is not acceptable.
